chapters.body:
The four maps share one way of moving. Cellar groups your wines by where they come from. Atlas is the wine world those wines belong to. Storage groups your bottles by where you keep them. Time Lens shows your cellar across time.

On a map, a larger tile holds more. In Cellar a tile is sized by the wines under that place; in Storage, by the bottles in that location, so a wine kept in two places appears on both.
chapters.title: Move around vynr

tour.message: Cellar, Atlas, Storage and Time Lens are maps of your wine, stacked one above the next.

shots.alt: Cellar: your wines as a map, grouped by where they come from.

callouts.text: Flick up with one finger to go to the next view.

shots.alt: Atlas, the wine world your bottles come from, one flick up from Cellar.

callouts.text: One flick moves one view: up goes on through Cellar, Atlas, Storage and Time Lens, then round again; down comes back. Storage joins once your bottles are kept in more than one place.

tour.title: Move around vynr

chapters.body:
The switcher lists the four maps — Cellar, Atlas, Storage and Time Lens — then Journal, Wine List, Producer List and Vynrpedia. Vynrpedia, the A to Z of wine terms, practices and places, is reached only from here.

Storage is always in the switcher, even before you have a storage location: it is where you add your first.
chapters.title: Jump straight to a view

tour.message: The switcher lists every view, both lists, Journal and Vynrpedia.

shots.alt: The switcher, listing Cellar, Atlas, Storage and Time Lens, the Wine and Producer Lists, Journal and Vynrpedia.

callouts.text: Drag up or down with one finger, slow down and hold: the switcher opens under your finger.
Keep your finger down, slide onto a view and lift to go there. Lift anywhere else to stay where you are.
Or tap the name of the view you are in to open the switcher; it stays open, and every row can be tapped.

tour.title: Jump straight to a view

chapters.body: On a list, in Journal and in Vynrpedia, one finger scrolls the page, so it cannot also move you between views. A two-finger drag is not a scroll, which is why the same hold reaches the switcher on every screen.
chapters.title: Two fingers work everywhere

tour.message: One finger moves you around wherever it isn't scrolling the page. Two fingers work on every screen, so where one finger scrolls, use two.

shots.alt: The Producer List, which scrolls with one finger.

callouts.text: Anywhere, drag up or down with two fingers and hold: the same switcher opens. On a list, in Journal or in Vynrpedia, where one finger scrolls, this is how you move.

shots.alt: Vynrpedia, the A to Z of wine words, which also scrolls with one finger.

callouts.text: Vynrpedia works the same way: hold with two fingers, then slide onto a view and lift.

tour.title: Two fingers work everywhere

chapters.body:
Swiping right from the left edge always means back: up one level on a map, or out of a wine's record. If a panel is open over the page, it closes first.

The count on a producer page, such as 3 of 12, is your place in the list you opened it from.
chapters.title: Go back, and across

tour.message: Sideways swipes work within what you are looking at; they never change the view.

shots.alt: A producer's page, opened from the Producer List.

callouts.text: Swipe right from the left edge to go back.
On a producer opened from a list, swipe left across the page for the next producer, or right for the one before.

shots.alt: The next producer in the list, one swipe later.

callouts.text: The count shows where you are in the list.

tour.title: Go back, and across

chapters.body:
Cellar shows only the places that hold your wines, so its map is shaped by your own collection: a continent appears when you hold a wine from it.

The bar is both the way in and the way back. Each place in it is a step you took, and tapping one returns you there in a single move, however deep you are.
chapters.title: Into a place, and back out

tour.message: Cellar and Atlas are maps of places within places: a continent holds its countries, a country its regions. The bar at the bottom shows where you are.

shots.alt: Atlas inside France, showing its regions; the bar at the bottom reads Europe, then France.

callouts.text: Tap a place on the map to go into it: Europe, then France, then Burgundy.
The bar at the bottom shows the way in. Tap an earlier place there, such as Europe, to go straight back up to it.

shots.alt: Atlas one level deeper, inside Burgundy; the bar reads Europe, France, Burgundy.

callouts.text: Press and hold a place in the bar, such as Burgundy, to learn about it.

shots.alt: The panel about Burgundy, opened by pressing and holding Burgundy in the bar, over the map of Burgundy.

callouts.text: Swipe right from the left edge to go up one level. Anything open over the map, like this panel, closes first.

shots.alt: Atlas at France again, one level up from Burgundy; the bar reads Europe, then France.

callouts.text: France again, one level up. Each edge swipe climbs one level; at the top of the map it does nothing.

tour.title: Into a place, and back out

chapters.body:
A hold explains whatever you hold. A place in the bar gives its story; in Storage, a tile gives the meaning of its storage profile.

Press-and-hold on words in vynr's own text is a separate option, Look Up Words, in Settings → Appearance. It is off until you turn it on, and while it is on, press and hold no longer selects text for copying.
chapters.title: Tap to go there, hold to learn

tour.message: Those are the two things a place can do, wherever its name appears. A tap goes there: into a place on the map, or back to an earlier one in the bar. Press and hold — keep your finger still — and vynr tells you what it is instead.

shots.alt: Atlas inside Burgundy. The bar at the bottom reads Europe, France, Burgundy, with a finger pressing and holding on Burgundy.

callouts.text: Press and hold a place in the bar at the bottom, such as Burgundy, and keep your finger still until it answers.

shots.alt: The panel that opens over the map after pressing and holding Burgundy, explaining what Burgundy is.

callouts.text: The panel explains the place you held — here, what Burgundy is. Every place in the bar at the bottom has one.
Swipe the panel down to close it. The map is where you left it.

tour.title: Tap to go there, hold to learn

chapters.body:
The list shows what the map shows. In France, the Wine List holds the wines under France; tap a place in the bar and the list follows.

Storage has no list: each of its tiles is a place where you keep bottles, and tapping one opens it.
chapters.title: From map to list

tour.message: In Cellar, the map can also be a list of the wines under the place you are in; in Atlas, a list of the producers at or below it. The list follows the bar at the bottom. Storage has no list.

shots.alt: Cellar as a map, grouped by country.

callouts.text: Spread two fingers apart on the map to see it as a list.

shots.alt: The same cellar as a list, one row per wine.

callouts.text: Pinch two fingers together on the list to go back to the map.
Or tap the view name and choose Wine List, or Producer List in Atlas; choose Cellar or Atlas to come back.

tour.title: From map to list

chapters.body:
After a scan, vynr shows what it read before anything is saved: origin, colour, structure and varietal, then details such as sweetness, when you acquired the wine and where it is stored. Correct anything that is wrong, then choose Add to Cellar, or Just a Tasting to record the wine without adding bottles.

If the wine may already be in your cellar, vynr asks whether to add to the existing wine, save it as a new one, or review first.

A free cellar holds 50 bottles at a time. Bottles you drink or give away free their space, and vynr+ has no limit.
chapters.title: Add a wine

tour.message: Every bottle starts from the + in the top bar.

shots.alt: The Wine List, with the add button in the top bar.

callouts.text: Tap + to scan a label with the camera.

shots.alt: The menu that opens when you press and hold the add button: Scan label, Enter manually, Quick Tasting and Start tasting event.

callouts.text: Press and hold + for more ways in: enter a wine by hand, record a quick tasting, or start a tasting event.

tour.title: Add a wine

chapters.body:
The Session narrows what you see for now; it never changes your wines. Pairing offers a dozen kinds of dish, from lean fish and shellfish to blue cheese and desserts.

Other sections appear when your wines support them: Sweetness, Opening status & intent, Notes, and Location once you keep bottles in two or more places. Clear session filters clears those sections; a pairing stays until you choose None.
chapters.title: Narrow what you see

tour.message: The Filters button at the bottom right of the Cellar opens your Session.

shots.alt: The bottom of the Cellar map, with the Filters button at the bottom right.

callouts.text: Tap Filters, at the bottom right, to open the Session panel; tap it again to close it.

shots.alt: The Session panel: Pairing, with a choice of foods, then the Cellar filters Colour and Structure.

callouts.text: Pairing: choose what you are eating, and vynr ranks the wines that suit it.
Under Cellar, Colour and Structure narrow the map to the wines you choose.

shots.alt: Further down the Session panel: Rating, and Grape / Varietal with a search field and the grapes in the cellar.

callouts.text: Rating and Grape / Varietal work the same way. The options reflect the wines you have, so a section appears only when your wines give it something to show.

tour.title: Narrow what you see

chapters.body: A producer page holds a short note on the producer, their ageing profile where vynr has one, where they are on the map, the other names they go by, and My wines when you own some of theirs.
chapters.title: Follow a wine to its maker and place

tour.message: A wine's record links to the people and places behind it.

shots.alt: The record of Alain Graillot Crozes-Hermitage 2022, with its map.

callouts.text: Tap the producer to open their page.
Tap the map to see where the wine comes from.
To come back, swipe right from the left edge.

shots.alt: The location bar at the bottom of the record, showing Crozes-Hermitage and the producer.

callouts.text: Tap a place in the bar at the bottom, such as Crozes-Hermitage, to see it in your cellar; press and hold it to learn about it.

tour.title: Follow a wine to its maker and place

chapters.body:
To add a location, open Storage from the switcher and tap + Add storage below the map. Name the place — for example, Basement rack — choose the profile that best describes its conditions, and tap Done. You can also create one from the storage row while adding a wine, or from a wine's record.

Once you have a storage location of your own, Storage joins the maps you flick through, between Atlas and Time Lens.

Each tile is one location, sized by the bottles in it. Tap a tile to open it: its conditions, the wines inside it, and the moves. You can move some or all of a wine's bottles to another location, or move everything out at once. A location can be removed only when it is empty. Press and hold a tile to learn what its profile means.

The profile — Ideal, Cool and stable, Normal indoor, Warm or variable, Refrigerated, Transit or Unknown — is the one setting that changes how vynr reads a wine's drinking window: the less steady the conditions, the wider the uncertainty, and a bottle keeps the widest it has known. Temperature, humidity and notes are kept as a record only.

A bottle added without a chosen location goes to the location you updated most recently, or to Default rack if you have none of your own. Every move is kept with its date, so your cellar's history includes where each bottle was. Storage is a map only, with no list, and it is part of the free plan.
chapters.summary: Storage is your cellar grouped by where the bottles are kept: a rack, a wine fridge, a friend's cellar.
chapters.title: Keep track of where your bottles are

chapters.body:
Memories is built from your own records: the bottles you added and opened, on the days you did it.

Evolution reads each wine's drinking window. Where a bottle has been kept affects how sure that reading is. Warm or variable, refrigerated, transit and unknown conditions widen it, and a bottle keeps the widest it has known: moving it somewhere steadier later does not narrow it again.

Your full history and the next six months are free; vynr+ follows every bottle as far ahead as its curve goes.
chapters.title: See your cellar through time

tour.message: Time Lens is the last of the stacked maps: flick up to it, or choose it in the switcher. Then tap a side.

shots.alt: Time Lens, with Memories on the left and Evolution on the right.

callouts.text: Tap Memories to go back through your cellar's history.
Tap Evolution to look ahead to how your wines will drink.

shots.alt: Memories in the Held reading: the bottles held at the date shown, grouped by country, above the timeline.

callouts.text: Held counts the bottles you held on the date you are looking at; Opened shows what you had opened.
Drag along the timeline to move through your history.

shots.alt: Evolution: when the wines in the cellar are expected to drink well, with the wines that are ready now named below.

callouts.text: Evolution charts when your wines will be ready; on the free plan you can look six months ahead.
Below it, vynr names which wines are ready now and which are still developing.

tour.title: See your cellar through time

chapters.body:
An entry holds text and photos. A free entry holds one text block and one photo block; more blocks in one entry are part of vynr+.

Journal can be narrowed to Tastings, Notes or Evolution. A tasting event gathers an evening's tastings under one name: press and hold + and choose Start tasting event, and every tasting recorded during it carries a Tasting Event badge.
chapters.title: Record what you drink

tour.message: From Cellar, Atlas, a list or Vynrpedia, swipe left from the right edge to open Journal. In Time Lens the edge swipe is not available: tap the view name at the top and choose Journal.

shots.alt: Journal, still empty, with the new-entry button in the top bar.

callouts.text: In Journal, tap + to write an entry.
Swipe right from the left edge to close Journal.

shots.alt: A new journal entry, with an optional title and the menu to add text or a photo.

callouts.text: Give the entry a title if you like.
Tap the + under the text box to add text or a photo; this menu opens.

shots.alt: Recording a tasting of Alain Graillot Crozes-Hermitage 2022: the taste glyph, a rating, notes and when you drank it.

callouts.text: To record a tasting, tap Tasting on a wine's record, or press and hold + and choose Quick Tasting.

shots.alt: Settings, showing Guide to vynr and the Full User Guide link.

callouts.text: Settings → Guide to vynr replays this guide.
Full User Guide opens vynr.app/guide.

tour.title: Record what you drink

chapters.body:
**There is no vynr account.** Your wines, tastings, journal and storage locations live on your device. vynr backs them up to your private iCloud account a few moments after each change, and only you can access that backup. Settings → Backup, in the Data section, shows its status and when it last ran.

**On a new device,** install vynr and open it. Before showing an empty cellar, vynr checks iCloud and restores yours. A backup made by a newer version of vynr asks you to update first.

**A copy of your own.** Export Cellar, on the same screen, saves your whole cellar as a .vynr file: wines, photos, tastings, collections and your journal. Restore from Backup replaces your entire cellar with a file's contents, and cannot be undone.

**What leaves your device.** AI Commentary and Refine Scans with AI are off until you turn them on in Settings → AI Features. AI Fix This and Cellar Health send a wine's label photo and details through vynr's own service, and only when you use them. Share Anonymous Usage Data, in Settings → Privacy, is off unless you turn it on. Assistant Link uploads a redacted, read-only copy of your cellar when you create a link and, while Keep my assistant up to date is on (it is on by default), again after each change to your cellar. Turn that off to publish by hand only; you can revoke the link at any time.

**Deleting.** Settings → Delete All Wine Data, in the Data section, removes your wines and saved label images from this device and from your iCloud backup. Your journal entries and storage locations stay. Deleting the app removes everything on the device; to stop backups as well, turn off iCloud for vynr in the iOS Settings app.
chapters.summary: Your cellar lives on your device and is backed up automatically to your private iCloud account; you can also keep a copy as a file.
chapters.title: Keep your cellar safe
